utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. The technical problems have been resolved. That does explain our late start. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Dreyer, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave yesterday when you started your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, are you ready to continue your examination in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dreyer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just for your information, I've spoken with Defence counsel so I think we'll proceed as efficiently as possible today, I think we have a reasonable chance of concluding today but certainly by tomorrow, I trust. Yesterday, Mr. Dreyer, when we concluded or as we were concluding the session, you had indicated the dots on P79, that's the aerial photo that you marked in 1996 and had explained the significance of those dots. I was concerned that might create some confusion as we can see on P79 there are areas, encircled areas that indicate areas of shelling, and then there are the dots which you indicated were specific impact locations both inside and outside those encircled areas. So I just wanted to give you an opportunity to explain the -- any difference between the encircled areas and the dots, whether that was a two-step process, essentially how it was that some of the impact locations ended up outside the encircled areas indicating areas of shelling.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've looked at the map very carefully over the last many, many years and looking at the dots, I mean the -- there was a time that I couldn't really understand what the dots were indicating and then there was areas where the circles were drawn as well. The dots, as far as I can recall, was areas where I physically seen the impacts, physically seen impacts happening as I was driving around and/or areas where I was while I was busy evacuating staff members where I saw impacts landing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the encircled areas are areas generally where you saw or experienced the shelling but didn't recall specific impact locations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, do the dots represent every shell impact that you saw or those that you recalled at the time you were creating the P79 in 1996?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dots do not recall every specific shell. The dots recall the shells that I specifically remembered at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And similarly the encircled areas indicating the areas of shelling indicate all of the areas of shelling that took place on August 4th, during your trips outside the compound or those that you recalled when you were -- specifically recall, that is, when you were creating P79 in 1996?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The encircled areas as indicated on the map indicates the areas where I saw smoke shelling or affected areas at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Finally I just wanted to make clear the relationship between the annexes to your 2008 statement which reflected the routes of the trip you took and the areas where you observed or experienced shelling and those would be P73 through P78 and P79. So do those -- well, let me ask you this: Was -- were these annexes reconstructions of the document that you created in 1996?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And they depict the same routes and the same encircled areas of shelling?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer, in paragraph 7 of your statement, you indicate that the attack on the 4th was led by multiple rocket launchers and heavy weapons in the form of 155-millimetre howitzer cannons. How did you recognise or identify those systems?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Multiple rocket launcher has got a very specific sound to it as they impact. 155-millimetre howitzer cannons, it could have been a variation of various cannons. I believe that the 155-millimetre howitzer cannons were either given to me by my own recollection or by speaking to the military, but the multiple rocket launcher's got a very unique sound to it as they come in, and it's unmistakable.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can we call up P79 once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer, I want to direct your attention to the encircled area to the left of the marking B. If we could enlarge the circle in the -- immediately to the left of B -- that's just below the -- yes, that's right. Mr. Dreyer, you can either look at it on screen or on the hard copy in front of you. There are four letters there which appear to begin with the letter M. Can you tell us what that says and what that's a reference to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, looking at it very closely right now, I believe it's MRL, which would represent multiple rocket launchers. But it's written there twice. I can't really make it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And can we enlarge it or -- if we can reduce the size sometimes it's clearer with the reduced size. You might want to look at it on the screen. I'm trying to find a resolution that's the most easily read, Mr. Dreyer. Sorry, I see you're looking at the hard copy. If you could address your attention to the screen.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Because there may be one resolution that makes it easier to read. Now, Mr. Dreyer, do you know whether or not -- that looks like a fairly good resolution. Do you know whether or not that is a reference to multiple rocket launcher systems rockets landing in that area, that encircled area?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that encircled area, yes, because at point G is where I was at 5.00 in the morning, excuse me, and the areas to our right and to our left was impacts of multiple rocket launchers, so yes, certainly, was there multiple rocket launcher in that area, to my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could also ask the registrar to enlarge the following area and perhaps it's best if I describe how to get there. If we could first direct the registrar's attention to where it says Knin at the top of the page, then go to the oblong below to the left, sorry, to the left there, and then to this first circle below that and then enlarge the enlarge the area, sorry, and into the smaller circle next to that to the left, and then if you could enlarge the area immediately to the left of that circle. That line running through the middle of the page, there are letters below the circle -- right almost at the top of the page, if you could slightly enlarge that. To the right. Yes, that's it. That may be a little too large but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, can you see the letters to which I was trying to direct the registrar's attention and can you read those letters for us, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They seem to me right now by looking at them, it seems to read MRL as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would that also be an area where you experienced or observed multiple rocket launcher impact?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I wrote it down there, that's what I experienced, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I see the Court looking so I want to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, just one small point of clarification. Yesterday you indicated that after the shelling commenced it took you about 20 minutes to get you back to the compound. I'm just wondering if you could give the Court some idea of how long that trip took under normal conditions.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under normal conditions, about two and a half minutes, two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In addition, Mr. Dreyer, you referred yesterday to a portion of your statement which referred to persons killed at the corner of the UN compound and to corrected fire directed toward those persons, that would be paragraph 19 of your statement. First of all, can you tell us what you meant by corrected fire?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. I'll try my best to explain what corrected fire is. Specifically, with mortar rounds, corrected fire is where fire is corrected by firing a single pipe or a single mortar round to direct it as close as possible to the target they intend to strike. I was standing inside the compound right next to I believe at the time next to the General and next to the Chief of Staff and we had a significant amount of civilian staff congregated outside on the corner of the UN building. We were I believe if I read my statement right, that was about 10.00 in the morning on the 5th. And what we saw was the first round of a mortar shell impacting further down the valley. Not long after that, there was a second shell that impacted closer towards us and closer towards the civilians outside the gate. If I recollect, there was a third round even closer and I realised, well, myself and the General looked at each other and we said they are busy correcting fire to hit the -- or to target the people outside the camp. And then the final round fell smack bang in the middle of the crowd outside the UN building, killing several of the people outside the building in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And just by way of clarification, you said in your answer there was a significant amount of civilian staff congregated outside the corner of the UN building, was that civilian staff or civilians generally?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say civilians, I mean they were dressed in civilian clothing so yes that's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know whether any of those who were killed on that occasion were in military uniform rather than in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In your statement at paragraph 15 regarding your fourth trip, you refer to a trip to Podkonje to try to rescue an UNMO team, that is UNMO Team Podkonje, being held hostage by Serb soldiers. First of all, by way of clarification, Podkonje is that area depicted in the aerial photographs to the right of the photograph? You'll have to answer --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, that's a yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How many Serb soldiers were you talking about on that occasion, how many Serb soldiers were involved in that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of them were dressed in military uniform. They were all dressed in civilians and civilian attire. But they were heavily armed and they were extremely threatening towards us. At one point we did believe that we were going to be under small arms and -- well, under attack from -- and that generally subsided after we struck a dialogue. I would say the number you're referring to, I would say anywhere between 6 to 10 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: These are formal unit people from Podkonje, how did -- could you tell what they were?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They looked to me -- at the time they looked to me like a small neighbourhood watch, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Also in your statement at paragraph 19, you mention that at about 5.25 on the morning of the 5th of August, the shelling recommenced with the same intensity as the previous day. When you refer to the same intensity, is that the same intensity as the shelling in the early morning hours of the previous day?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The early hours of the previous day, I was in the middle of the shelling, so for me, the intensity was heavy. The following day I was observing the shelling and from a distance, I would say that the shelling was what I perceived or what I could see over Knin was of the same intensity, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And were you able to observe what parts of the city the shelling on the 5th encompassed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a vantage point from where we were seated in the UN building by overlooking the entire valley. As previously explained, the areas on the right which I could not -- I didn't witness myself, but basically we were looking out over the entire valley of Knin and as you can see in my sketch and in the map, that that's the area that could have -- that we observed. So yes, we were looking over the entire and the -- I would say whether -- I wasn't in the areas but I would say the shelling was predominantly downtown, but certainly in the areas indicated as well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, on either the 4th or the 5th of August, did you see any outgoing fire from Knin toward Croatian positions or toward advancing Croatian troops?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniquely, as I previously indicated on my map as well, I did see a mortar position indicated on the map as C, but apart from that, in all honesty, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that mortar position you referred to, did you see it firing or you saw the position?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the position. I saw it being manned. They were certainly active. Did I see firing from it? No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, in your final paragraph of your 2008 statement, as indicated yesterday, you make reference to finding dead civilians, most of which had been shot at close range. As you heard yesterday, the Court was interested in as much specific information about those observations as you are able to provide, so I would ask you to provide as much information as you can about what you observed, when you saw it and where you saw it. Perhaps you can begin by telling us, with reference to those dead civilians, the specific observations that you can recall making.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the -- what was said yesterday referenced the final paragraph and my indication that I've seen tens of dead. There is no reason for me to exaggerate on how many dead people I've seen, to be quite frank. We were driving around. We've seen -- if I say tens, it was basically that I couldn't recount exactly how many people I saw that was dead, but certainly there was a substantial amount of dead people that we found in various locations as we were driving around. Some of them were old. I recall seeing a man that was definitely in his late 70s. There was a woman, she was definitely in her 70s. They were all shot at close range. I'm not saying by whom. I'm saying they were shot at close range. The two I referred to just now were shot through the head. We found a shallow grave with a man with his hands tied behind his back. He was shot through the head. On the road leading from Knin out on the mountain oust road leading towards Zagreb, we found at least three or four different bodies lying at the side of the road. They were stripped off their clothing, they had their underwear and T-shirts on. They were shot at close range. Within the town of Knin, I think we found one or two. But predominantly it was on the outskirts of the city of Knin themselves where we did observe several dead people, women and men at various ages, none of them dressed in military uniform and shot at close range. Now, it's very difficult for me to explain it in any more detail than that, but that is exactly what we've observed. And it was not only me, there was several people with me, so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when or approximately when, even if it's a rough time frame, you made these observations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think what I referred to in my statement, the first time we really went out -- the first time that I went out on my first non-rescue related mission was on the 6th of August but on the 9th of August specifically, we were driving around to various villages looking at the extent of the damage. Apart from the dead that we've seen, the dead humans that we've seen, we've also observed almost all cattle, dogs, all animals, pigs, everything was shot in the process as well, so yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Dreyer, you indicated that the encircled areas and the dots representing specific shell impact locations were provided to the best of your recollection at the time but did not represent all of the shelling that took place. You've also explained that on August 4th, during the course of the day, you were travelling essentially the length and breadth of Knin from one end of town to the other. Let me ask you this: As far as you could tell on that day, was there any part of the town that was safe from shelling?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think what I did is at the time when I drew this map, I was asked to indicate as specifically as I possibly could recall on where the shelling affected different areas within Knin. On your question was anywhere in Knin safe at the time while I was driving around for the duration of the 4th of August, my answer to your question would be no. What I did over here is I was really trying to be as specific as I could. What I should have done is I should have taken a big pen and drawn a circle right around Knin and not specify and say: This is the area of impact. Because that was the area of impact. Knin itself, in all directions where I travelled, at any given time during the 4th of August, my life and the life of my staff members were at peril.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dreyer. Your Honours, one final matter. Prosecution has generated some maps that make the alphabetical markings and that also consolidate the information contained in the annexes into one document. I provided them to the Defence. Mr. Kehoe asked in particular asked for an opportunity to review those to make sure they indeed conform with the other exhibits but we would like to present those to the Court assuming there's no objection and we'll -- I'm sure that we'll hear from the Defence on that. Otherwise, Your Honour, I've completed my examination in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These -- as a matter of fact, they were provided to the Chamber already, so these are the I'd say the civilised versions of the trips.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then we use them to assist us in understanding fully P78, I think, because it's extracted from that one, all the trips.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll use them. They're not in evidence but if there is any -- apart from objections, if there is any inaccuracy in it, for example, I noticed that if the trip says it moves this direction, that direction, then what were two lines now has become one line but that is clear without further explanation. So if there is any inaccuracy we would like to hear. Otherwise, we'll for practical purposes use these maps. Please proceed. Yes, Mr. Tieger, that was your examination in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have one question for you. You referred to 20 minutes to return. I had some difficulties in finding that reference to the 20 minutes. Was it in the statement, was it in the testimony of yesterday? Because it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was in yesterday's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday's testimony at page ... I could search for -- I can search for minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was on page 1723 at line 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I have one problem ... I have not yet the new version of yesterday's transcript but with the word we'll ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And 20 is in the transcript numerically, Your Honour, rather than written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's yesterday's transcript, the old page numbering is 107:22. Mr. Dreyer, could you indicate exactly -- you said it took you 20 minutes to get back to the UN compound. It's position G, I now see. Yes. I found it. Thank you very much. The sequence of cross-examination, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I give you an opportunity [French spoken]. Yes. Judge Gwaunza first has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dreyer, if I could take you back to paragraph 19 of your written statement on page 6 at the top, the last-but-one sentence of that paragraph at the top. Are you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the top, ma'am, at paragraph 14 or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Page 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: But the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am, at the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: On page 6, yes. You said, "The bodies of the victims were placed in body bags by our soldiers, only to be removed by Croatians and driven over by their tanks." Could you explain that what you meant by driven over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can, ma'am. What happened was when the -- when the mortar round impacted on the site of the UN building on the road, several people were killed. I believe that I indicated five to six, I believe. We were not allowed at that point on the 1st to leave the compound but the Canadian soldiers were. They took some body bags, they went outside and they placed the dead inside body bags and they placed the body bags on the side of the road and returned to the camp. Only later for -- when the Croatian military actually arrived at the edge of the compound for some of the bodies to be removed from the side of the road and driven over by tanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still not entirely clear. You said, "Some of the bodies to be removed." So may I then take it that some of these body bags were taken by Croatian soldiers and loaded on to whatever and then taken away and that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour. It means that the body bags --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- as they were with the bodies inside were taken from the side of the road, placed in the road, and then driven over by tanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I understand. They were put on the road, tanks would come, drive over the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- bodies. Yes. That clarifies it. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will be the first one to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will be the first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dreyer, you will be cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe, who is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dreyer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you get my messages where we had been attempting to speak to you for some time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've received your messages. Do you want me to clarify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you get the various messages from counsel at UNICEF that we were trying to concept you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you did not agree to any such conversation with General Gotovina's Defence team, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not up to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you some questions about that particular time in Sector South. You were the UN security coordinator for Sector South; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And how long were you in that job as of August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the specific in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the specific position in Knin.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had you ever been a security coordinator prior to that time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And where had you been a security coordinator?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And during what period of time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: About six months leading towards that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned in your statement that you had been in the South African Defence force. Had you been in combat prior to this?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you define combat, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Combat where there is shooting fired in anger, if you will?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within South African territories.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please observe a pause between question and answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, going back to the time that you spent in Knin -- May I have one moment, Your Honour. So you became the security coordinator in approximately June of 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And during that time, virtually every male in that area was part of the army of the Serb Krajina; weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not up for me to say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, isn't it a fact, sir, that that -- virtually every male up to -- into the 50s had been brought into the army of the Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's -- no, I've got no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I mean when you were in your job as the security coordinator, did you have regular meetings within the compound to assess what was going on in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did that include exactly what was transpiring not only on the Serb Krajina side, but also on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Transpiring from which perspective, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Either militarily or troop movement wise or what was happening in the area.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had that kind of knowledge, I wouldn't been racing downtown Knin 5.00 in the morning trying to get my staff, so yes, I did have -- I did meet with military commanders, we did meet with the police. We did use the military itself. But did I have specific information that you are referring to, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. So let me show you a video that is ID15-0064. It is -- excuse me, I'm sorry, it is 3070 -- I'm sorry, which one is this? Here it is, ID 150063, that's the B/C/S and -- this is a video from TV in Belgrade up to Serb Krajina generals, General Novakovic and Sekulic, S-e-k-u-l-i-c.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "In fact, the average age of the army of Serbian Krajina is 47 years. These were indeed already middle aged people. I calculated the average age in several companies that I observed and the average age of the companies was 56 and the average age in the brigade composed of such companies was 53 years."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, when you were talking about matters within the UN compound, were you aware of the ages of the men in the RSK and that men in their -- into their 50s and older were part of the army of the Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So that was -- that was not a matter that was discussed on the UN compound?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not part of my responsibilities. My responsibilities included the safety and security of the United Nations personnel in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And part of the safety and security of the United Nations personnel in Knin was knowing who the armed elements were on both sides; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, but not the age of the armed element.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, in order to know the size of the armed elements, it's important to know the individual characteristics of those elements, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually not. My responsibility did not include the -- to dissect exactly what the military forces was comprised of. My responsibility was to make sure that I make sure that my staff were safe and my staff was alive at the end of the day to go back home. So the age groups of the individual soldiers within the military was not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we will offer this video into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not on the record, I take it but -- yes, no objection. Even without a microphone, your voice is heard clearly, Mr. Tieger. Then Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that becomes Exhibit D101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D101 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, were you aware that virtually the entire population in Knin prior to Operation Storm on the 4th of August was armed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, where the military supply depots were in the area?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware where the factories in the area that were producing military supplies were?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us talk a little bit, and we'll go through this quickly, about the period of time just prior to Operation Storm. You were aware that the Milan Martic of the Krajina Serbs declared war on the 28th of July of 1995; weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware that Grahovo fell to the HV forces on the 29th of January -- July, excuse me?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's 14 years ago. In all honesty, what you're saying now, I believe I did, but if I had any knowledge of the situation that the advancing forces were going to invade Knin, my staff would have been in compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would not have been living in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand that, sir, but you're aware Grahovo fell on the 29th?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the specific dates, no, I can't recollect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Approximately?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were you aware that shortly after that that the Serb civilian population began to leave in buses, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly asked to make pauses between questions and answers, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you observe that after the fall of Grahovo that the Krajina Serb employees on the UN compound, many of them stopped coming to work?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is not correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you were aware that you did observe, and I point to paragraph 3 of your February 2008 statement, you were aware that around August the 1st, you saw RSK tanks, six or seven RSK tanks moving towards the front line?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what front line were they moving towards?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were moving towards the front line indicated by the military to us, we didn't know exactly where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you get an idea where the front line was going?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So are you telling us that prior to the 4th of August, you had no indication that war was coming?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try and say this again. If I had any knowledge whatsoever that an invading force was coming to Knin, my staff members and the code that the country was operating underneath our security regulations would not have been in orange, it would have been in red. My staff would not have been in their civilian residence and they would have been in the UN compound if we had any indication that this was coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact -- I'm sorry, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm getting a little ahead of myself, Your Honour, just waiting to catch up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact, sir, that after the fall of Grahovo, you advised the personnel in the UN compound that were living outside the compound to keep a bag packed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recollect, but I certainly did advise them. It's part of our security planning, we do that all the time, we advise staff to keep a bag packed under stage green.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So are you saying that -- when did you go to stage orange?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in stage orange at the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when did you advise these people that they should keep a bag packed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is part of our normal procedures. We advise them to keep a bag packed whenever they go to a regular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you told them to keep a bag packed all the time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: United Nations staff is always advised to have a bag packed ready for relocation at all times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you yourself move to the compound at some point?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall, but it was certainly before the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Approximately when?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say a couple of days before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And so if -- we're talking about the 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but -- I can't recall, but certainly ahead of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did other people move to the compound at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some people did, specifically people with responsibility that had them at work more than regular hours, so it was just preferable to stay within the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So with people coming into the compound --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Take a breath now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, sir, so after -- sometime several days before the Operation Storm, people were coming in the compound; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you had no knowledge that there was any discussion that some type of war -- that some type of fighting was going to take place, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fighting was going on. We knew fighting was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And where was the fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fighting was happening at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where was the front line?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, we were relying --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- definitely and wholeheartedly on the military that was assigned to us recommendations where it was. So at that point in time, the front line was not close to Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the front line is up by the Dinara mountains, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm asking you, sir. You were there.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The front line was certainly an area that was in the vicinity, but was it to close to Knin to my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, prior to the morning of the 4th, did you receive information from any of the UN staff that an attack was going to take place at 5.00 in the morning of the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Prior to the morning of the 4th of August, 1995, were you informed that an attack was going to take place by HV forces on 4 August 1995 at approximately 5.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I clarify. Are you referring to a date before the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: A date before the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection today, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if information to that level came into UN Sector South headquarters prior to August the 4th, you were not informed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that information came into Sector South headquarters that Knin was going to be attacked prior to the 4th of August, 5.00 in the morning, I was not informed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who made the decision -- I apologise. Who made the decision as to when the alert level was going to go from orange to red?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision on the alert levels at that point in time was in the hands of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who in the military?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military within our compound it rested with the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff at the time was Colonel Leslie.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, when was the last time you spoke to General Leslie?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that he was a General. As far as I recall, he's a Colonel, and the last time I spoke to him was in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would be in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the military made the decision to go -- make that change from orange to red; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when was that change made?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I read back at my statement and to the best of my recollection, that decision was made 4.00 in the morning on the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And there was never any indication prior to 4.00 in the morning on the 4th of August, now I'm talking about from the night before until 4.00, there was never any indication prior to 4.00 in the morning on the 4th of August that anything was going to happen at 5.00 a.m.; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to my knowledge or to the knowledge of anybody else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm referring only to your knowledge, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My knowledge, no. My only recollection was 4.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, on this particular point, during your time there, did the Republic of Serb Krajina ever declare that the city of Knin was a demilitarised city?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know what I demilitarised city is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where no military is present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No military is present, no military activity.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they declared it a demilitarised city, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You don't know that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You spent time in the armed forces yourself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you are aware of military targets, are you not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And would you consider army barracks military targets?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Police stations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending in which context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What context are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Which context are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm examining your question, Mr. Dreyer. Is a police station in Knin a military target?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the police station in my opinion was armed, if the police station was hostile, then yes. If there was no one there and the police station was not hostile, then certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about the headquarters of the Main Staff of the army, would you consider that a military target?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reference back to my previous answer, again, hostility intent, how many people was present, the answer would be if they were hostile, yes; if they were not, then no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You would agree with me, would you not, that the headquarters of the Main Staff of the army is the central point of an army, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's manned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If it's manned or unmanned, if they have equipment in there or anything else, that particular headquarters is the main central locale for an army, isn't it, the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly depends on what's around it and what's in it. If you're referring to whether I believe that the central headquarters of a military is a legitimate target, my answer is it depends what's inside of it, how aggressive it is and what's around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. And when -- let's take that point, what's around it. And you would agree as a military person that military authorities should not put a military target in an area where civilians lives, should they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military targets in -- military headquarters in many countries, including the one that we are in, is around civilian targets. It's just the nature of the layout of a city.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So your answer to the question is putting a military headquarters in and among a civilian area housed by civilians is okay?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, military headquarters around the globe is housed around civilian areas. Now, as I previously tried to explain to you, if the military headquarters was an aggressive front line military headquarters, it's a different story. But a lot of military headquarters are a place of -- where people come generally to do work. It's not necessarily an aggressive force, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about a military headquarters when that country has declared war?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What does that mean? Does that then --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Does that render it a military target?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I go back to what I said? If it was hostile, if it was hostile, sure. If it wasn't, then no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about communication centres, sir, is that a legitimate military target?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We'll go back to it. If the communications centre was part of the aggression and part of the threat, then certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about factories that are involved in making military supplies?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on what the factories are making, are they making military supplies in the form of first aid kits, are they making military supplies in the form of band-aids, are they making bombs, I mean, it all depends on what the factory is delivering.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So your answer to that question is it all depends on what factories are delivering?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, and if the factory is active.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's us turn to your first exhibit, if we may. And I think it's -- not the first one. Let's just go to P79.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It might be easier to read, Mr. Monkhouse, if we go to P73. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, P73 -- I'm sorry. Do you have that with you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. P73 is the trip -- your first trip; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one I'm looking at the screen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can just blow up the bottom part of that page coming out of the UN compound. If we can blow up that just a little bit more around the parliament building. We can just shift it over a little bit to the right. I'm sorry, I meant to the left. That's good. Now, that area, that's the street, main street going down Knin, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you identified that as an area that had been shelled during the period of time that you went out on the 4th of August on your first trip.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And by the way, your first trip out, that was with you and Mr. DeKlerk?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you took two soft-skinned vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there anyone else from the UN compound with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe we had -- in each vehicle we had a Jordanian soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, taking a look in that area, and we're looking at the area to the parliament, I'd like to address your attention to Exhibit D20. I'm sorry, D20. If we can blow that up just into one, please. Now, sir, that is a photograph from behind the street that you drove down on your first trip out of the complex, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, really. I've never seen this before. If you can indicate to me where the street is, I can help you out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if can look, if you can look -- you see where the railway is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you can just drift into that street, you see it on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You see the street and just follow it up.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's the main street, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the picture, that's what it appears to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, on that main street that you indicate was being shelled, is a series of buildings identified to the left as the buildings complex of the Main Staff of the ARSK, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. If you show me the picture -- if you say it is, then -- I don't know. I wasn't aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were not aware that that was the headquarters or the Main Staff headquarters of the army of the Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this picture before. I'm not quite sure even if the picture, I recognise the picture. But if -- I don't even know on the map exactly where the picture is at. It seems to me like it's closer towards the beginning of the railway station. On the map that I have it seems to be the parliament building. No, I wasn't aware that that entire complex was, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware that the Main Staff had their headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention to D -- excuse me, I take that back, 1D15-0068.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just go into private session for 30 seconds just by a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer, to orient you with this photograph, do you recognise this overhead of Knin going down the main street?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And this is the main street that you went down, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if you agree with me, just going through these targets in this locale, the -- you see over in one on the right-hand side is the military barracks Senjak, you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And number two is the bridge location. And by the way, just looking at that bridge location in number two, you're familiar with the bridge location there and the tunnel, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you know that there was a tunnel in and around the bridge location number two where the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina had an armoured train to travel on the rails with anti-aircraft weaponry and other anti-personnel weaponry? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that specific location, two, no, but I have seen the train, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell us a little bit about this train.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually saw the train after the 4th of August, way after the 4th of August and I didn't -- the understanding that I had and that I think most of us had at the time was the train was not Serbian, that the train was Croatian. I didn't understand that the train was actually was Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it could have been Croatian after the 5th of August, but I'm talking about prior to that.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw it prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So you were unaware that that train -- that the Serbs had that train in that tunnel around two?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the train that you did see obviously could move on the tracks, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the tracks, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go to three. Number three is an intersection in and through Knin, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You're aware of that location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, sometimes the -- not only the speed of speech but also the speed of thought goes beyond my abilities. We're talking about a train. The witness says: "I have not seen that train before the 4th of August," he said, "but I saw an armoured train far after the 4th of August." Now, you are in your questions implicitly drawing conclusions that it was the same train and then you say it was on the tracks, which is highly suggestive for the Chamber to know about a train that was there on the 4th of August or around the 4th of August, but if we have not established that it's the same train, all conclusions about what the witness saw later and he says was it a Croatian train and where you suggested that it might be the same, and of course I can follow that suggestion. But then to move on with the speed of a train, I would say, and then to suggest that what was valid for the one train is valid for the other train as well needs precise exploration rather than ... So therefore, I'm -- please try to understand what this Chamber has to do; that if you want us to believe that something was true for the train you say, we didn't know whether it was or not but the witness certainly did not confirm that, was there around the 4th of August, that you can't just go to another train or the same train without having established whether it was the same train or not. And in your questions, it's all implied and that may be a trial technique but it certainly doesn't assist the Chamber in precisely and carefully considering what evidence comes to us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Frankly, it's the tension between complete clarity and expediency and trying to move the matter along, frankly, and I understand some of the scheduling issues and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Expediency usually asks that you -- that you are selective and, for example, not ask the same question twice or three times, as happened this morning only at least a couple of times. So therefore you can gain a lot of time there and then gain precision on other matters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, just clarifying the train situation, where did you see the train that you saw, observed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the train on the train tracks at the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The railway station in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And can you describe it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you say, it was quite unique. I've never seen anything like it before. It was an armoured train. Did I see the weaponry on it, the anti-aircraft weapons you're referring to, no, but certainly it looked like a menacing train, sure. Did I know who the train belonged to, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the train tracks, this was at the train tracks in downtown Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go back to the exhibit that's on the screen and turn our attention to point 5 and that is in fact the main railway station. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that where you saw this train?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember if it was exactly at 5 or possibly further up the track but it was certainly in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not looking for precision in that, just the general area.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not in general area 5, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It was not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say. Like I tried to explain, it was certainly on the railway tracks. It was certainly in Knin. Whether it was specifically at 5, the answer is I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Number 6, this is the particular area that we discussed in Exhibit D20, and number 7 is the parliament and government building. Were you aware of that location along the road?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, number 9 is known as the seniors' home. Were you aware of what that building was used for?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you know where ARSK soldiers and -- excuse me, officers were staying when they came to Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, number 10 is a railroad -- excuse me, a railway communications centre. Are you aware of that location?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the building that is known as the 11, old hospital building, were you aware of the use by that by ARSK military?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Finally, you can see the number 12 on the edge of this photograph which is the TVIK factory; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the right-hand side. And that was a factory that was in Knin and was hit by artillery at the time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was hit by artillery but I know it was a factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you did circle it in your map, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can just give me a second. Can you indicate to me on my map where it is, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry sir, could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you indicate to me on my map where the TVIK factory is, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sure. If you travel up your map from B up past H, it is to the right of your letter H.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is two circles, there is a large circle and a small circle. Are you referring to the large circle?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, then it was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know that was a factory?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it was a factory, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, did you want to take the normal break now or did you want to continue or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it depends. We -- we could have a break a bit later, but that means only that we have shorter sessions later on so therefore, if this would be a suitable moment for you, then we would have a break and if you would like to continue for a couple of minutes, it's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's -- I'm going to move to another exhibit at this point so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take the break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. At this time, the Defence would like to offer into evidence 1D15-0068, the item that's on the screen entitled "Fired planned targets".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit D102.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it based on earlier events that there is no objection. Then it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to refer back to the train issue and I do have a new video taken by TV Montenegro in Knin. I do not have -- because it came up, I didn't have the audio. I will get the audio at a later time. The only item I would like to do at this point is show it to the witness and ask if he can identify this as the train.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we need the audio? I take it that the audio will explain what it is and isn't it true that -- I don't know, but it might be, whereas this witness of course, I take it that you him to compare what he has seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the actual, you know, video itself. The audio at a later juncture, as long as I can get square with the interpretation that everybody has the correct interpretation, I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have no transcript of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Not at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's impossible for the interpreters to interpret without having a transcript, especially when the speed of speech is such that -- if you say they are talking very slowly ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I misspoke. I'm not going to play the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are not going to play the audio.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. I was just saying that there is audio, I'm not going to play the audio because I don't the transcript and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then I misunderstood you. Then we'll look at the video and -- without paying any attention to the audio. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, you had the opportunity to review that video. Does that appear to be the train?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really see anything. I saw the two people being interviewed, that's it. But what I can say is the train that I saw, I took a picture of it so I've got a picture of the train that I saw and if I can recollect, it had a Croatian emblem on the side of the -- on the train. This train did not appear to be the train that I saw. I just don't know, I didn't see enough of the train to be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we'll offer this video into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the video is admitted into evidence. Whatever probative value to be attached to it at this moment, Mr. Kehoe, is -- we know that there was a train and there were two people interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will tell you, Judge, that I will enhance the weight of this exhibit as time moves on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you say you'll find other evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that will corroborate this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any way -- would it be of any use to ask the witness or would you have any information which we would then receive in evidence as to who the people were who were interviewed? Usually if you're so close to a train, you have got something to do with that train and I saw uniformed people. I'm not able to identify what kind of uniforms or what army they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They were Krajina Serb military personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's at least that's what you want to present evidence on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As an officer of the Court, I can present that to you. I will tie that up at a later date but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer, I'd like to take you through a series of slides, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- one additional question because otherwise -- do you know when this footage was filmed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It appears to be taken --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It appears to have been taken in Knin in -- sometime in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. It will be tendered, no objections but, a number has not been assigned to it. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D103 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Now, if I may turn to -- it is 1D15-0021 and it goes through 1D15-0042.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, I'd like to take you through some of these slides, if we can. And it will refer back to the maps that you drew and some of the locations that you testified about as well as identified in your statement. So please feel free to refer back to the hard copies that you have before you. Okay?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page of this document -- can you just blow that up just a little bit. At you can orient the Court, you recognise this overhead, do you not, as the city of Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you just orient the Court as to using the cursor and maybe with the assistance of the usher we could do that just a bit. Just looking at this photograph, I mean if you can just point with an X as to where the UN compound was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, we've seen and heard that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. We can just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not 20 times, then 30 times. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if everybody is oriented, that's fine. Let us move to the next slide then. That's the first slide. The next slide.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dreyer, take a look at this slide and these are the areas that you circled in your exhibits; is that right? And I'm talking about P79.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that any different from my map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I submit to you that it's not and I certainly hope that it's not. It was an attempt to be as accurate as possible with the items that you put on your map.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will take me some time to go over it but by looking at it briefly, it certainly seems that you've captured most of the areas, if not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I ask you, sir, if as we're going through this, if you see anything that we got wrong, could you please correct us?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, excuse me. I suppose I asked this question and it is a question rather than an objection per se. But I don't understand why we're using a replica of another exhibit that purports to be the same exhibit and contain the same information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exactly, because it's not the same, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you look at -- if you look, for example, at letter G, which originally was outside the area where it's now inside an area, it's relocated -- the letter G is relocated in comparison with the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason why the replication takes place will become clear as I move through these slides. I don't think there's any question that when the witness was talking about the letter G, he's talking about an area that is generally in that locale. I certainly will move that G outside that if need be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not -- the letter G is not where it was, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's what I'm saying. I mean we have now a different version and you said you hoped that it was exactly the same. It's not. And I have -- that's just on first sight, so therefore, I think the question put by Mr. Tieger: Why not use the one produced by the witness if it's not exactly the same, this one, I would prefer to go to the original then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I will -- if I can go through this and I will change that as need be. I certainly can move that G outside that. It was nothing more than an oversight, simply at this juncture. It was not meant to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but what does it add to present a new version of exactly the same? Apparently. I think the only change that's changed a bit are the colours, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's purple now where it used to be red, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge and if I'm permitted to go through this, we can certainly refer back to the Prosecution's exhibit but if I can go through the particular slides that I have in this particular fashion, I can make the appropriate changes on that. And any other change that Mr. Dreyer maintains should be made. But for the sake of moving through the questioning at this point, if we could move through this slide -- these slides that I have prepared in this juncture, I will make the appropriate corrections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what I do not understand, Mr. Kehoe, that if it's exactly the same, then I do not see why this would work any better. But Mr. Tieger, instead of spending another ten minutes on which copy to be used, or to be strong objection against proceeding as Mr. Kehoe -- I mean, it's clear that it doesn't make the Chamber very happy what happens at this moment, but at the same time, if we could proceed. But, Mr. Kehoe, if at any later stage we find similar matters, then you have less time for cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Other than the -- thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Other than the particular area that's noted as the G, I mean is basically the other matters consistent?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From looking at it initially, yes. But now that G -- there might be some other differences but I mean like you said, if we encounter them as we go, I'll let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us move to the next slide.
