Now, sir, I have identified in yellow and I will identify further some of the areas and they are marked in yellow and I have noted them as military targets. And other than the inclusion of that, you understand that that's an overlay over your particular marks that you had put in your document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, is it true that the map you present at this moment goes far beyond the map that was marked by this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's the second difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is -- what I am attempting to do here is track the -- this particular item, as I put on the bottom there, are areas referred to by the Witness Dreyer and then I have marked in yellow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- military targets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So we will get into those, sir, but you see -- observe those yellow targets?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the yellow. Whether they were targets or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the yellow, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can move on to the next item. This is essentially, sir, an item where we have put yellow pins in areas that are designated as the military targets. If we could go to the next slide. You see them out the particular circles. And now the next slide. Now, sir, I have attempted to identify some of the items that are in there. Of course we have previously talked about the northern barracks, and that is in one of the pins that's under the names, but let me just go through some of these items as we talk about it. And looking at the top, are you familiar with the factories up in the Kninjanka, and that's up at the northern part of the map? Do you know that that makes military supplies and manufactures military supplies and is a storage for the military?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just make an observation on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The areas indicated in purple versus the areas indicated in yellow, the yellow pins are relatively much larger than the orange pins. Can we -- it's just not in perspective to for me to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What I hope to designate because it actually is going to get quite crowded, I put those pins -- the purple pins in there to show the general areas that you have circled because we are going to put more information on this as we overlay, and I invite you at any point, please, to go back to your original map.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So you have no idea what's made as the Kninjanka depot; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about if you move to the right to the Dizel depot, do you know that was the headquarters of the state security service and also a rail yard?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you show on my map where it is. I can see on your map where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you agree that is the Dizel depot as both a rail yard and the headquarters of the state security service?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. If we can go back to the slide. Now, moving down to the bottom part, there is a depot called the depot Krka and -- which is a military storage area at the bottom portion of that. Are you familiar with that as a military storage facility?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I look at my map and I look at your map, that's not even in my map.

utterances.text: I'm just asking if you're familiar with that area.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]

utterances.text: That has already been dealt with. I already told Mr. Kehoe that we have a map of a larger area at this moment on our screen. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the other area that I would like to just highlight is on the left-hand side of that, which is the residential building of Milan Martic. Were you aware of Milan -- well, first of all, were you aware that Milan Martic was the president of the Republic of Serb Krajina?

utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were you aware that he lived at that location?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, one question about the retirement home which is two names down --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, can I ask you a question. Which ones of the pins represents his residence, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You see the highlighted yellow right next to the t-i-c?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right there, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now the retirement home, do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On your map, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know whether that was used as a operation facility by Milan Martic prior to and on the 4th of August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, isn't it true that you have asked this question already in relation of a different matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The retirement home, you asked whether the witness was aware what it was used for. The witness answered that he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I just altered the question to ask him if he knew that Martic was using it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do not know what it's used for, then you certainly would not know these kind of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will move on, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the next slide, which is your -- a tracking of your first trip through Knin. Now, comparing that to the -- your originals, that is roughly the area that you went through, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let's turn to the next slide. And these are some of the areas in larger circles where you indicated that you either saw or observed detonations; right? And you can compare it to your map.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly on the road where I was at where location G is on the map here, where location G is, I was actually there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So at location G right there, I mean certainly we experienced large amount of explosions because that's exactly where we were and that's where the indications on your map in purple is some of the specific impact points, yes, but there was certainly more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. I mean in a larger area as you put in your map?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go to the next slide. Now, I put the -- what the Defence submits are military targets in -- back in the pins and followed it along your track. utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were military targets --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- you're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to this -- now, this is the first trip that you took at 6.00 in the morning -- excuse me, I'm sorry, at 4.40 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right. Now, your second trip was when, your second trip, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at my --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Please take your time. You can refer back to your statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second trip, 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, could I ask you one thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see this to be the second trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is -- on the screen is the first trip, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's the first -- yes, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It should be designated at the top, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any reason why the -- apparently the white itinerary is strong -- is strong white at certain portions where in other portions, it's hardly visible? utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's a distinction in intensity of the white in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, there is none, frankly. I mean other than that's how it came out on the computer. We could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It could be that -- I don't know how it's produced by a computer that smaller roads are depicted by less intense lines and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is certainly a smaller road back behind there. There is no question about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is meant to designate the area that he went back, if you recall in his statement, that he went back in a different fashion, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, on the way back to the camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, let us turn our attention to the second trip and let me get down to the next slide. Now, again, what time of day was this? You were going to refer back to your statement on the time of this second trip.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I answered that. 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misheard.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just looking at my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's okay. All right. Who did you go with?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second trip was done, if I read my statement over here, we took two Jordanian APCs. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So in -- was he in your APC or the other APC?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't recall but I believe he was in the second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall any other UN personnel besides the Jordanians, you and Mr. Dawes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was leaving the compound?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall but certainly we picked people up along the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And those were the ones that you were extracting from the various locations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can take this second trip and if you look down at the item that's on the -- or the slide that's on the screen, can you take a look at that, that would basically represent your --

utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, is everything -- is the whole itinerary indicated here? I'm trying to find and I'm using at this moment the -- this map with the bright colours.

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would look with me on -- and perhaps compare these two maps. If you would look with me to the area, and perhaps we would zoom in so that we have a better idea. Now, if I look at the second trip map where with colour it's highlighted, then I see a green feature somewhere in the middle of this area. I would very much like -- as a matter of fact, yes, where the at this moment the cursor is, I find part of the second itinerary there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I do not see it reflected on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I think that is an oversight on my part and as I look at that, that is an oversight. I think that the actual -- absent that, the actual path that we're following here and the methodology that I'm employing will basically encompass that and I can certainly correct it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I can see it in one minute, why can't you see if in a couple of hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I plead guilty. I just -- I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have no specific response to that. I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact, I cannot establish at this moment that there's no factual basis for your plea. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can continue that other than the correction that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this may be of assistance. I'm not sure this is related to the series of questions Mr. Kehoe intends to ask, but it's a point I would have clarified in redirect, if necessary, but there's no point in embedding the issue prematurely, and that was the witness referred to his statement with reference to who accompanied him on the second trip. And I note that the way the statement is formatted places the third trip not -- above the description of the third trip on the page and so there may have been a confusion between the second and third trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No. While I missed the issue that Your Honour suggested, I did catch the issue that Mr. Tieger presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not guilty, therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Not guilty -- I don't think there's -- if you see, I think what Mr. Tieger is talking about is right below the signature on page 4, the computer put third trip down there when third trip should be at the top of the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct, and my impression was that the witness was referring to the continuation on page 5, thinking that that was the second trip that he was attempting to respond to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So do you want to clarify that then, sir, on the second trip?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By looking at my statement, yes, I would like to clarify that it seems that Mr. Dawes was not with me at the second trip, that he was only with me at the third trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who was with you on the second trip?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had two Jordanian APCs, so it will be Jordanian soldiers and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was Mr. DeKlerk with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the second trip?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the second trip.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I can recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So it was you and the two Jordanians?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So just going back to this second trip, we see the item that's on the screen with a correction pointed out by Judge Orie, and if we can go down to the next line. And again, I've place, and I know it's in a larger area, the items that you refer to as detonation areas on your second trip. And then let us turn to the next slide. Now, sir, this second trip which began about 6.00, again, in a large part of this, if these are military targets, you were again driving through military targets to get to the UN personnel to extract them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By looking at your map and looking at your description of military targets, I would say more than 70 per cent of that trip was not at military targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So then that would be the northern portion of it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But the bottom portion of that where the yellow pins are would be if there was -- you would be driving through an area, if those were military targets?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bottom part in downtown Knin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the shelling was going on in that area during your second trip, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shelling was going on, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the red dots on the itinerary is -- reflect exactly what? I'm a bit con --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the path -- the little purple pins, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The red dots on the white lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's just the path taken as opposed to -- if you look aside, Judge from the actual roads that you see to the left of that and the right of that, it's just attempting to show the path that Mr. Dreyer took while he was moving through that area and it's just an attempt to segregate it from the roads that he didn't use there. Because you see on the left and right-hand portion of that slide that there were roads that he didn't travel that particular trip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that the red dots just highlight the roads he took?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, that's all it does, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's an attempt to follow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that trip went from 6.00 to approximately when?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the -- on my statement it says that the trip started at 6.00 and it doesn't give a time of conclusion but it certainly says that my third trip started at 8.30 so I presume just before 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And when you came back after -- how many people did you get on this second trip?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you went back did you report to anybody?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went back into barracks?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I report anything into barracks of who I got from the city of Knin? Is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Or did you discuss with anyone back in UN Sector South headquarters what was going on out there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who did you talk to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in my statement over here that I went to the bunker and I discussed with the sector commander and the Chief of Staff but I'm sure that I -- I also reported to my supervisor, which was the chief of administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would have been General Forand and Colonel Leslie?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You then took a third trip; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And approximately what time of day was that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Referring back to my statement, it indicates that I departed at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And do you recall who you went with at that time? And you can refer back to your statement.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reading my statement paragraph 14, it indicates that I changed from the Jordanian APCs to Czech APCs and it refers I took Mr. Dawes with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So that would be Murray Dawes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be Murray Dawes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And so it was you and two Czech drivers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could have had an escort in the vehicles with us. I just can't recollect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you, Mr. Dawes and the Czechs. Anybody else in those APCs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at this trip. And by the way, was it during this trip, sir, that you ran into some Krajina Serb soldiers who attempted to take your APC; do you recall that? It's not in your statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, but I remember -- I remember the incident you're referring to, I just don't remember on which trip it was, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, tell us about the incident first.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see in my statement it was the fourth trip when I went to Podkonje but if you look on the map it's on the right top-hand corner. We were informed, as far as I can recollect, that there was an UNMO team stuck in Podkonje and we needed to -- and we were asked to see if we can retrieve the UNMO team in Podkonje. We did. We utilised a Czech APC. It was not far. It was on the same route that I normally ran in the morning. And it was just around the corner. We drove into the small little village of Podkonje and I was in the turret area looking out. I believe I had a Canadian soldier with me and a Czech driver, and as we drove into Podkonje, I think I observed them first, there was two guys in the trees, in the bushes with shoulder-mounted anti-personnel weapons with them and AK-47s and various people on both sides of the road hiding in the bush and I thought we were going to be attacked. I told the driver to stop, which we did, it was a very tense 10, 15-minute standoff between us and them. We eventually were asked to get out of our APCs, which we did. We were offered coffee. We asked whether we could retrieve the team in Podkonje and we were told no. And we returned back to Sector South headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Who was the Canadian soldier that was with you, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was on your fourth trip?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Via my statement, it was my fourth trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go back to your third trip that we have on the screen here and again, I have attempted to map the area that you went through.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, which trip is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The third.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is the trip that you said began at 8.00, correct, with Mr. Dawes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 8.30, apologise. With Mr. Dawes and the Czechs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let's go through the first slide. If we can go to the next slide. I have attempted, I recognise those areas are larger on your chart and if we can go to get the following slides --

utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, did you fill in the part of the itinerary which does not appear on the original maps and that you have chosen your own solution for where the witness went?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe, Judge, that from the statement, we went through and on this particular chart, came -- he came back and back around in the other direction. So I --

utterances.text: You thought it must have been the road you indicated here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Because of the logical area of what he said during the course of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I will ask him that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Logic -- yes, we'll ask the witness whether -- could you have, perhaps, a look at -- yes, especially the left part, whether that is the route -- the road you took because it does not appear on the original maps, I think, at least on D75, we can't -- no, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And 75, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's not complete. It's an area which is beyond the map and Mr. Kehoe has logically filled in that part of your itinerary. Has he done that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just taking a look at this slide, again, absent the left side of this slide and the top side, when you were again travelling through the centre of town up past the southern barracks and the Tvik factory, if these are the military targets, you were driving right through an area that was covered by military targets; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were military targets, and by looking at it seems like about 70 per cent of the trip was not close to military targets, but if they were, yes, the first part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the fourth trip that day, and referring back to your statement, what time was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And tell us about that, sir. How did you go, who was with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By reading my statement on the fourth trip, it doesn't indicate who was with me but I -- it would be my deduction that it was with the Czech APCs. Whether anybody specifically was with me, I can't recall. And what happened is by reading this, I went to Podkonje and then from Podkonje, we couldn't rescue the UNMO team and then we proceeded back into Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So taking this particular chart and moving it on the fourth, and this is 12.30, how long did this take?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says -- at the bottom of my statement it says, "We returned from this trip at approximately 1500 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just taking us through this particular -- the fourth trip and going to the next slide. Again, I have placed your particular areas with the idea that your areas encircled are larger. If we can go to the next slide.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I might make an observation. On this trip, the trip to Podkonje is not included.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And this particular area, I was just going through the areas of military targets.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And I apologise for that because I will talk about the Podkonje trip in one moment.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the area -- the area that you're going through absent the trip to Podkonje, and we will go back to P76 in a moment which shows that trip to Podkonje, again, if you were in this particular area that you travelled, when you were travelling downtown in these various buildings, you were driving -- if they are military targets, you were driving through an area of military targets that were again being shelled; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were military targets, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, also in this fourth trip you took this trip to Podkonje; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you were going through there, did you observe any ARSK, army of the Republic of Serb Krajina, any military at all during this time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the whole day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, during this particular trip or during the whole day. Let's start from the whole day and then go in this particular trip.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I indicated in my statement that I did see a mortar platoon. I saw an APC, I saw a turned over militia vehicle but apart from that heavy presence of RSK, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see RSK trucks moving around?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you not see with Mr. Dawes four RSK trucks coming back down from the direction of Strmica road?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. I didn't mention in my statement so I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see any truck movements whatsoever of RSK trucks moving around?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can refer back to my statement of what I wrote at the time. It's 14 years ago, so it is -- if I did see military vehicles it would have been more the odd military vehicle than the presence of military vehicles. So there was no large presence of military in Knin that I observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me go back to the -- if I might have a moment, Your Honour. If I can go back to 1D10-0084, if I can bring that up on the screen. This is a video from Associated Press TV taken on the 4th of August from the headquarters -- the UN headquarters in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, does that -- were you in those APCs or looking outside the turret in either one of those, do you know?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been me, yeah. It doesn't look clear but it could very well have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The one on the left with the white shirt on, I know it's difficult to see?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You observed -- stop. You observed trucks like that moving through Knin on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was behind me. I didn't see it. Well, did I see trucks like that specifically? There could have been the odd one but not the -- like I said, there wasn't the presence of trucks all over Knin. There might have been the odd one, but yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see -- well, I take it back. That's fine. During the course of the time that you were there, did you run into soldiers from this brigade called the ear-ring brigade?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The what de.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The ear-ring, ear-ring brigade.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you observe soldiers when you were with Mr. Dawes, soldiers coming back from Strmica back into Knin, ARSK soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can't recall. If I didn't mention it in my statement, then I don't believe I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the shelling that you were talking about, there was shelling going on not only by the HV but there was shelling also taking place by the RSK soldiers too, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if I can just go to the -- If I can number this first, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes D104 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, that's the previous video shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This one. Okay. I didn't have it on the screen. I'm sorry. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D104 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You of course know General Forand; do you not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you said that when you were coming back to the headquarters, you were coming back to the Sector South headquarters, you were talking to General Forand and to Chief of Staff Leslie; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I spoke to General Forand directly, I can't recall, but Chief of Staff Colonel Leslie, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you the next -- it's actually a continuation of this video by -- also by AP TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, could we just stop for a moment? Just a housekeeping matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: My -- and I don't think it's important in this particular instance, but I registered no objection to what I thought was the entirety of the exhibit that was being submitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was the -- I at least understood that to be the beginning where we see two people on an --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will split this up into two separate exhibits. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can take this from the beginning again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You recognise General Forand, do you not? Mr. Dreyer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] "In the area of responsibility there is a lot of shelling from the Dinara mountains and responding Serb artillery fire in the Dinara mountain. I think we have lost a crossing point which was called Pakovo Selo."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, he talks about shelling, Serb shelling going into the Dinara mountain. Were you aware of that on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said from the Dinara mountains. I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go back and play it again. We'll go back and play it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] "As you go south in the Kenyan area of responsibility, there is a lot of shelling from the Dinara mountains and responding Serb artillery fire ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He's talking about Serb artillery in the Dinara mountain?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Kenyan controlled area, the Kenyan controlled area was not downtown Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, but it was in fact Serb artillery firing, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, not that I observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, but that does seem to raise a point the Court raised earlier, and that was whether or not the question implies something that is not in fact embedded in the document or previous evidence and this is a question about Serb artillery fire. The witness had made a distinction about Serb fire in the area of -- in the Kenyan area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact, Mr. Kehoe, it's always good if it's not the witness who has to point at imprecision --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- rather than counsel to be so precise, there is no need for a witness ever to point at overlooking something in the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And Your Honour, and I will submit to you that there is evidence of Serb artillery in and around the area, not just this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not saying that, but you show this to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you have not laid a foundation as to what extent the witness personally observed and then you ask questions in relation to what was shown to him which is a -- a technique which requires extreme caution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And especially under those circumstances you are invited to take care that it's not the witness who should correct imprecision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if I may, if I may, there is also follow-up questions to this about the level of discussion within the UN compound about Serb artillery. It's not firing of Serb artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What will come, we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But here it's quite clear you put a question in which you left out a detail of what we saw on the video and the witness said, well, this is what it said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And my submission, Your Honour, is that I was not completed with follow-up questions from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you say this was not in the area. Did you have discussions in the headquarters about the Serbs firing back with their artillery at the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might have. But did I see artillery fire being fired on my trips - I believe that's what I'm testifying, from my trips - did I see artillery fire, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you understand my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. My question to you is: Did you -- excuse me. Did you have discussions in headquarters about the Serbs firing back with their artillery at the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From which specific area?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Any area.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might have. I can't recall. I might have sat in the meeting where it was discussed, but I didn't observe it. That's my entity. I didn't see it downtown Knin as I was travelling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was not whether you observed it. The question was whether you were aware of any discussions about it and you have given your answer by now, that is, that it may well be but that you do not recall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during this trip to Podkonje that you took on the fourth trip and if I can refer to your P76. Now, looking at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue with that, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Tieger, you provided us with a fourth trip assistance map, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that is supposed to reflect what we find in this fourth map as it is now on our screen, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It certainly should.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Same comments as far as the Defence is concerned. utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't see that on mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The Court's comments are -- first of all, I understand the point. You're completely right. We will not only modify this, but we'll conduct a review of each one of those demonstrative documents and not resubmit them until they are thoroughly scrutinised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In terms of guilty please, it's one thing --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, I'll plead guilty for him, too, just in one fell swoop, I'll take his as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, of course, if within half an hour we see these kind of differences, that really means that someone has done some sloppy work and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will not spend any more time to it. I add just one more thing, Mr. Kehoe, I am still surprised -- I'm still puzzled by the red dots on the itinerary, because if I would have to highlight an itinerary with red dots, I would put them at an equal distance approximately and not ten in one centimetre and then three in the next five centimetres. So therefore it still puzzles me whether your explanation can convince me, but I still do not know what else it could be, so at this moment we leave it as it is, but let's try to be very careful not to start redacting what witnesses have given us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will get a more cogent explanation. That was my understanding. And certainly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you get a another, a better explanation, because earlier, you referred to logic. I miss the logic in it. Let's not spend any more time on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this trip shows your trip up to Podkonje, it that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in this particular trip, and if we go up and we could put on the screen D5, this is a situation report, an UNMO situation report from August the 4th at 1600. I believe it's -- excuse me a second. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just scroll down just a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can look at paragraph 6, this reflects the situation in Podkonje with the RSK soldiers holding UN personnel hostage; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, did you ask me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just take a look at 6. I'll just have you take a look. It's easier if you just read it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, you went to Podkonje on the fourth trip and RSK soldiers were holding UN personnel hostage, were they not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they were RSK soldiers. They were armed men, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: They were armed men. You did say in your statement, as I recall, and I refer to paragraph 15 of P72, "At approximately 1230, we embarked on our fourth trip when we initially went to Podkonje to try and rescue UNMO Team Podkonje who were essentially being held hostage by the Serb soldiers in the town." You did say that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the individuals that you described as Serb soldiers were dressed in civilian clothing, according to your testimony that you gave this morning?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at my statement, I would believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. But you concluded at the time when you saw these armed men that they were, in fact, soldiers, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's turn back to the slides and talk a little bit about the fifth trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, do I have to bring that back, it's 1D15-0021 to 1D15-0042. And we're going to the fifth trip. Can you go on to the next one? That's the fourth trip. Can we go to the next one. Now, again, if we can just blow that up just a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can, Mr. Dreyer, taking a look at this and you'll see the particular route, I believe, is consistent with the route that you took on your fifth trip, and you can check back with your documents if it is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only part of the trip that's not accurate is the road leading through downtown Knin. I can see on my map as well, it seems like they separated it but the whole idea is I went down one street and came back through the same street through downtown Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the lower aspect of that is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I just went through downtown Knin out to the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll correct that. If we just note that you followed the main street up, turned around and came back on the same street.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll correct that. Let's turn to the next slide. And by the way, I don't think I asked you, on this fifth trip, tell me, again, the fifth trip, who did you go with and what time did you go?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Referring back to my statement, it indicates that I left after 1500 hours with one Czech APC. It seems that it was me and a Czech driver or maybe an escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And do you remember who was in the escort?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Dawes go with you on this trip?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So as far as you recall, it was just you and a Czech driver and the APC and what type of escort would you have?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would most likely have been soldiers, if I can recollect, soldiers within the vehicle to protect us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And do you have any idea who those soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And let's just take us through again looking at the fifth trip and using the smaller areas that you had previously marked, knowing full well that your were larger. Let us turn to the next slide from there. And again, putting -- if these are military targets where the pins are there, as you are driving downtown on this trip, both back and forth, if these are military targets, you were driving through an area that has -- that is being shelled.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they were military targets, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time if I could offer into evidence this particular item, this particular slide show that we have and I will make the appropriate corrections consistent with what Your Honour has pointed out and likewise what Mr. Dreyer has pointed out with regard to trip 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He yes. And perhaps you could provide for our verification a hard copy of this fifth trip as corrected and also a hard copy of the other --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- slide that should be corrected so that we have a quick reference to your corrections. Mr. Tieger, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the slide show would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D105 is admitted into evidence subject to the corrections to be made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, any other trips that day other than the five trips that we talked about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that as you were travelling through many of these areas downtown, you were being -- driving through areas that were being shelled consistently?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say consistently but they were other -- I observed shelling, I observed impacts or I observed damage caused by impacts, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you were driving through them?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during your entire -- by the way, you went there to pick up UN personnel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It became a bit more complex than that. It became from UN personnel, international staff, to national staff, to national staff's parents. It became a bit of a -- it diverted from what it was intended to initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was any UN personnel or any of these people killed during any of these extractions?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During any of these trips that you made, did Colonel Leslie -- do you recall Colonel Leslie accompanying you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's talk a little bit about the situation after the 5th. Now, you maintain in your paragraph, and I believe this is paragraph 8, you maintain that all RSK military elements had withdrawn as of the 5th of August. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. How much shelling was actually done by the RSK during the 5th into Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the RSK into Knin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, can you -- are you asking how much shelling was done by the RSK into Knin on the 1st?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On the 5th, on the 5th of August, any time during the day on the 5th of August, are you aware that the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina was shelling Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to Defence Exhibit 89. If we can turn to one, two, three, four pages in. The third paragraph down, at 1500 hours. That's it. If we can read that, Mr. Dreyer, "At about 051500 hours," and I can tell you that this is a sitrep for the 5th, "ARSK soldiers of unknown strength were seen occupying defensive positions in general area of Strmica XJ 00 91. Tanks and mortars were seen in the same positions. At 051815, they fired 12 rounds of artillery from Strmica towards Knin." Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions in your headquarters with either General Forand or Colonel Leslie or others about the ARSK fighting back?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fighting back?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Fighting. Returning fire or fighting back against the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And did they tell you that they had information that the ARSK were in fact putting up a fight?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I believe they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, the -- did you have information about -- do you know who General Mrksic is, the commander in chief of the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn, if we can, to 65 ter 47426. This is a transcript of an interview with General Mrksic delivered to Radio Belgrade at 2100 hours on the 4th. It notes that -- if I could just read it down you can read it with me, radio Belgrade journalist. "The aggression which commenced at 0500," this is General Mrksic speaking, "the aggression which commenced at 0500 lasted until the nightfall. At the present, all combat activities in the area had Knin have ceased. Knin is enveloped by the dark, evacuation of the population is ongoing. Enemy forces reached at four to six kilometres from the city." Question: "Does that mean our lines have been penetrated?" Answer: "No, we are maintaining contact, our forces withdrew to the positions for the direct defence of Knin. The other range units are still successfully holding their positions." We can move down to the next paragraph, approximately one, two, three, four, five -- seven lines from the bottom beginning "if." "If the army of the Republika Srpska succeeds in putting pressure on the forces attacking in direction Grahovo-Knin, we shall then stabilize the defence and switch on to counterattack." Now, Mr. Dreyer, was that consistent with the information that you and the other UN personnel at Sector South headquarters had concerning the fight that the army of the Serb Krajina was putting up against the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my concern at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was that consistent with what you heard and what you were talking about in Sector South headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's not. Did you not just tell us that you understood that the army of the Serb Krajina was putting up a fight against the Croatian army? Did you not tell us that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. But not in this detail. This is the first time I've seen this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we will offer this document into evidence. It is 65 ter 426.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D106.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Dawes [sic], turning -- staying with the 5th, it is a fact that there were troops returning from the front lines through Knin, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just reading your question again just to make sure that I understand what you're saying. You're saying that on the 5th is it a fact that the troops were coming from the front lines through Knin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true as far as I can recollect. I was busy within the headquarters. Whether troops were moving in and out on the 5th, I was not allowed to leave the compound, so I cannot answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So from the compound, did you observe ARSK mechanised units and trucks moving down the road up through Knin?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me turn our attention to one other item. You know, you said from the discussion on direct examination that you went out briefly on the 9th -- excuse me, on the 6th and then you went out a bit more extensively on the 9th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recollect, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And sir, this is the best of your recollection, I understand this is a long time ago. Honestly. So during the period of time that you were there, and when did you leave the Sector South?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When did I physically leave Sector South?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Approximately. You don't have --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think December.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: December 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During that time, sir, did you in fact do an analysis of the shelling of Knin by going around the entire area to see what was in fact damaged?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's me bring up a document for you, Prosecution Exhibit 64, if we can put that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you know and individual by Lieutenant-Colonel Steinar Hjertnes as a UN military observer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to paragraph 1 and 2, if you could take a quick look at that, it notes that "UN Team Podkonje has made a provisional assessment of the damages caused by the HV operation 04-06 August 1995 in the town of Knin. The report is based on a rundown of 70 per cent of Knin town and gives only a brief overview of the situation. "In general, shelling was concentrated against military objectives. The damages caused by shelling to civilian establishments is concentrated to the close vicinity of military objectives. Only few (3-5) impacts is observed in other urban areas." Were you familiar, sir, with this assessment done by the UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the final assessment done approximately a week later that was consistent with this assessment?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this assessment before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me turn our attention to the area that -- one area with some video that you talked about certainly on your first trip. If we can go back to this map and what we're talking about is, if I may, I believe it's P73. If we could bring P73 back up.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.text: Do you recognise that fuel station, that petrol station there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My answer to this, Judge, is that this is WTN TV and the matter was turned on and off. This particular area of the road is the one readily identifiable as --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe it starts just north of the Tvik factory.

utterances.text: Yes. Now you pointed -- that's the reason why I asked for the cursor to be there. You pointed at a place which was what I described as a fork and could be somewhere else. I do now understand that further on you consider this to be the road downtown.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is a road, Judge, if you look just up from the --

utterances.text: -- there is a road by the grid mark that comes up and that's the left, they come down on that road.

utterances.text: They come down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You see that road just right above the grid mark there, they come down that road and then make a left down the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, but I asked you what I see on this map is that is what I described as a fork, that is that you have to choose left or right from where we came, whereas what I saw on the screen was ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think if you go back up there, Judge, you can see that the road can continue on on top of that wooded area there and then -- this is of course a rural area, or you can make the left down that road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On the screen where the car turns to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is an option to go straight ahead as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I do believe it's there. You see it, it's not a straight line, it looks like a little bump that you can go straight up. You see the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not spend more time on it. Please proceed.

utterances.text: Now, sir, you do remember this area?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You do not.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recognise on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continue on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recognise these buildings, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you place yourself on this street at all?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, for me it looks like any village within the area. I don't know whether this is a specific street. If you say it's a specific street then I believe you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm trying to get the idea of this is the street where you state that the shelling started when -- on the morning of the 4th of August of 1995, and I'm just getting and idea if this is the -- if you recall this and when you mark in your chart about buildings being hit and artillery coming in, I just want to get an idea if these are in fact the places where you saw this artillery being hit. Is this or isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your purpose is perfectly clear, Mr. Kehoe, and the witness said, "I do not recognise the street." So let's go on and see whether there comes a point where he does recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We'll just continue on, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Instead of -- it's perfectly clear what you are aiming at. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continue on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this turn into town, sir? Did you recognise that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It again looks very familiar, but I cannot say that it's strikingly recognizable, no.

utterances.text: Let's go to the next video, then. Maybe it will be clearer. Now, this video --

utterances.text: If the might have the assistance of the usher again.

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you take -- can you take the first -- okay. And this, if you keep going on, that's the main road going through and as you're looking over to the left is the train station --

utterances.text: Excuse me, that's perfectly clear. I just wanted to know the last turn seems to be a 90 degrees turn to the left. You can choose to go to the right or to the left but there's no straight ahead. Where exactly is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where the cursor is right now.

utterances.text: Where the cursor is right now. The cursor is now over the railway bridge as far as I can see, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And you make that bend around that way on to the main street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to understand. Are you saying that coming from or -- I'm always a bit confused by this map -- this road which goes from south-east to north-west into the town, that there is a 90-degree turn just before you go to the railway bridge? Is that how I have to understand it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It comes as -- you see from the screen here, Judge, it almost comes to a dead end that you see there with the buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you turn to the left because you can't go straight on. Then from what I understand, then, some 50 or 100 metres further to the left you come to the railway bridge. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can just have a number for this, Your Honour, and move this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D107 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I can take you to the next video. Again, it is from also WTV and -- WTN, excuse me, and that is a number of 1D15-0067. Again it's a WTN video from 7 August 1995 and it's coming from the opposite direction. Now, one reference point here is looking back down at the town and the other reference is going back up the road we just came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that street, Mr. Dreyer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The street that we're talking about is a wooded street with vehicles coming in both directions. Do you recognise this area generally at the crossroads in town?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that area, Mr. Dreyer, and that building?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continue on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise the barracks on the left-hand side of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to find my position on -- by watching the video. I'm trying my best to figure out where I am over here. utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Just continue on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about those buildings, sir? Do you recognise those buildings?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.text: Continue on.

utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]

utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, I do have to correct a matter that came up with regard to the maps and I can show a little bit more accurately the videos.
