I have been advised by my staff that that's how that video went. I was under the mistaken impression --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, it's totally unclear. Could you tell us first of all where the bus takes the left turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's up -- if we could now put the cursor up to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, further up to the right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right, right, right, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Further to the right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right there. Makes a left-hand turn down that street. It's coming from the right and makes -- goes to that corner and makes a left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, so that's a totally different --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Totally different, Judge, I was mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then the video cuts off and then retakes it as we come back down into Knin town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That also means that we see fragments of that road not -- we have not a complete picture of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We don't have a complete picture. The TV camera shut off until we come to the road back into Knin and we go down the road and then make the turn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just by way of clarity, I apologise for that, I just wanted to make that perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, just one last question, we talked a bit about the shelling on October 5th, 1995 outside of the camp that you discussed in paragraph 19 of your statement which is P72. And I want to bring up on the screen P69, photographs that have been admitted into evidence by the Prosecution. This would be pages 06067511 -- I'm sorry. I've been advised, Your Honour, to go to page 3. If we can take a look at these photographs. First these two, and these are photographs that have been admitted into evidence which note at the top, "Two of the six bodies which sustained fatal wounds." And if we can go to the following page. You see, sir, that the individual that is lying on his back on the top page has a camouflage jacket on?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Can we just blow up the bottom picture. And you see the camouflage as well as what looks like some type of military holster or a holster on his waist; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the holster but I cannot see the camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. But you can see the holster?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the holster.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Now, when the -- you noted for us that Canadian soldiers went out to attend to these bodies?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When they came back, did they tell you that the wagon that they were -- that these individuals were on was filled with weapons?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you talk at all to Sergeant Engelby, the Canadian Sergeant Engelby?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall Sergeant Engelby. Did I discuss whether there was weapons on the truck, I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You had no such discussion with Sergeant Engelby?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall if I did but I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, you made a proffer that is set forth in paragraph 19 going on to top of page 60 that the Chamber has asked you questions about, and I will tender to the bar that there are and I have looked during the break at at least two autopsies concerning these individuals that have been identified and I will, from the bar, tender those autopsies and submit to Your Honour that they will not be consistent with what Your Honours heard today concerning the running over of tanks. So we will do that when we pull those together and tender them across the bar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, I have no objection to tendering documents across the bar. I'd just like to see the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They are documents that the Prosecution has given us and we will go through them and agree to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are aware of what documents Mr. Kehoe is referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not specifically. That's my only point. I'm sure there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And just by way of clarity so there's no mistake, I mean we obviously went through the documents to identify these individuals and then match these individuals to autopsy reports that were done by the medical examiner and of course looked at those in detail and those would be the items that we will tender across the bar and certainly I will discuss them with counsel before I do so. Still, you are developing thoughts which are -- so what we'll receive then are autopsy reports which are supposedly linked to the events this witness described --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that is persons being put in body bags --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And being run over by tanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know exactly what is the relation to this one, whether that's the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is this incident, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is all the same incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know that yet. I've seen this material and I've heard the testimony of the witness and I have no one seen or established that this is the same, I think. Is it? Let me just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think that that -- this is the same incident, is it not, Mr. Dreyer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen these pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The incident that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a mistake on the transcript in page 92, line 11 who speaks, but it might be that I've missed something that it has been the testimony of this witness that the matters you show as pictures now is the same event as he described where he says, "I've never seen these pictures." I don't know exactly on what basis I have to assume that it's the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I frankly don't think that's being disputed by the Prosecution that these photographs are photographs of the incident -- they were put in as such as P69 and identified as such that they were put in as the mortar shelling that took place on 5 August 1995 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's where the witness said that it was adjusted to come closer and closer. Mr. Tieger, is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the smaller issue regarding the precision of the documents earlier, I want to make sure I'm as precise as possible so I will look this over more carefully. However, Mr. Kehoe is correct, I'm only aware of one such incident. I believe we are talking about the same incident but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the Judges do not have an overview over everything that still will come, so therefore, it's the only one or whether there were others is -- we are not aware of that. So if you tender them from the bar table, Mr. Kehoe, then we don't have to urgently deal with the matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and Mr. Tieger takes his time to see whether there is any objection against that material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One point of clarity, Your Honour, that I have talked to Mr. Tieger about and just for the sake of efficiency, if you will, we did get a D number for a video which is D104 which is the two APCs coming into the headquarters with the truck driving past. How we had presented -- coming in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that wasn't clear to me. I see that they go through a gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But whether they go in or out is -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe they're coming in. In that same video with that TV station, the next clip is with General Forand. I talked with Mr. Tieger about it and asked if we could just put that in with one D number, which is D104 as opposed to creating another one and I don't think that Mr. Tieger objects in any fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So D104 and -- D -- D104 and D105 are merged then is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We never got a D number for D105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It will be one where you indicated that it will be two separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar then the ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's correct, so the video with the document ID 1D10-0084 remains Exhibit D104 and includes the entire video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I do understand there are no objections, Mr. Tieger. Therefore D104 is admitted into evidence in its new identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. Mr. Dreyer, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who was next --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic, who is counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Dreyer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, you had stated in your earlier testimony that the security of your personnel was your job number one; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it would be rather important under the circumstances to know the situation in and around Knin to be able to adequately prepare security for your people; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You had earlier stated that you knew that the town in Bosnia, Bosansko Grahovo had fallen but you weren't sure of the date; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that what I stated?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I believe that's what you said. I can go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is any issue with that, please quote Mr. Dreyer literally, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. On page 20, line 15, the question was: "I understand that, sir, but you are aware that Grahovo fell on the 29th. Answer: "On the specific dates, I can't recall, yes."

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you were aware that Grahovo fell but you're just not exactly when; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether Grahovo fell or not. I'm sure I was informed of it, recalling it right now, but all military information, all the operational information was received from the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Honours, I'd like to ask the usher to open up map 15, and if you would do so as well, Your Honours, the map in the map packet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that in evidence, that map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is not, Your Honour. It is for demonstrative purposes only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Map 15, perhaps it could be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I would ask the usher to do. You can use mine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, you have the map in front of you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And there is a pointer that the usher has given to you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I'd like you to refocus the map so it shows further down. There we go. A little further. That's good. Now I'd like it focused a bit, please. Hopefully it's not my eyes that are unfocused. Is it visible on the ELMO, Your Honours for you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not entirely but I've got map 15 next to me so --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We're almost there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It appears to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, do you see the town of Bosansko Grahovo on the right there just north-west -- or north-east of Knin? There is a small dot.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could you put the pointer there, please. Okay. Now could you put the pointer at Knin. I'll submit to you and I'd like you to assume that Bosansko Grahovo fell on the 29th of July of 1995, okay, for purposes of this question. You see the -- this is the Prosecution's map, by the way. Do you see the line in between Knin and Bosansko Grahovo, I believe it's reddish-brown?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you point to it, please. Were you aware that that line was the front line the day before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the bottom left of that map, there's a scale. And if we could sharpen the focus a little bit for everyone on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, can I ask you one thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're looking at this map and you say it was the confrontation line the day before Operation Storm, do you mean at the start of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's clear, because that was on the day of Operation Storm was the 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, do you see the scale there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we focus it a little bit more, please. Thank you. The top scale is in kilometres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it's in the first -- it's 0 to 10 on the first top of the portion of the scale; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If you could go back to Knin and Bosansko Grahovo again, please, and refocus on that area, please, Mr. Usher. Okay. Now, right above the arrow that's pointing toward Knin, there's a little point that juts out, do you see that point on the reddish-brown line, Mr. Dreyer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this area specifically there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Using the scale, it's -- and I'm not going to be exactly precise. I know Your Honour wants precision. But the front line was roughly as the crow flies at that point about 10 kilometres from Knin; was it not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears so on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So at least the day before Operation Storm, the confrontation line for security purposes was 10 miles -- or 10 kilometres from Knin; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as you explained it on the map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You can put that down. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, was this your first awareness of how close the front was to Knin before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you to refer to your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one thing. I think the witness made a reservation that he said "As far as I can see on the map."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So awareness of being so close, I understand at this moment that to be in terms of the earlier portion of the evidence of the witness that as we did with the military targets that if this was the confrontation line that your awareness of it being so close comes today for the first time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you're correct. If I might have a minute to explain. Just on reference to confrontation lines, et cetera, it's been said that I was responsible for the safety and security of the staff, which I was, but on the military information we had no military information at hand or any mechanism of doing so, so I had no idea of the line of confrontation until that morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, I'm making this observation because the witness testified several times that he hardly knew anything about the confrontation line but now for the first day looking at this map on the assumption that that's the confrontation line, the witness now becomes aware of the closeness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to prefer to P72, Mr. Dreyer, your statement of 21 and 22 February, 2008. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Counsel, do you have a copy for Mr. Dreyer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 2008, excuse me, it's in front of me excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, on the front page of that statement P72, and I would ask that that be please pulled up if it hasn't already. Actually, the cover page I'd like, please. Thank you. You were interviewed on February 21st and 22nd of this year; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's less than three months ago?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the events that took place during Operation Storm were about 12 and a half years ago; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If you go to the last page, please. Your signature appears on the last page dated February 22nd of '08; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you when you signed the acknowledgment?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This specific one on the 22nd of February?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in New York city.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you were visited by members of the Office of the Prosecutor to conduct these interviews?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In New York city?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to refer to the top of page 6 of that same statement. You describe and Mr. Kehoe cross-examined you on the issue of the mortar round; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What type of mortar was it, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- okay. It wasn't an artillery shell from a howitzer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When you talk about a mortar round, what kind of range would that mortar round have, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on which mortar round was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you're not sure which mortar round was used; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be my presumption it was 80-81-millimetre mortar that was used but it could have been smaller. I don't know what mortar rounds were available, but to my knowledge, it would have been in the 80s range.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What is the range of that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The other point that you referenced in this paragraph which was -- which has been discussed is the issue of the body bags; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then in paragraph 22 you discuss additional observations which you expounded on in your testimony. The additional observations in paragraph 22 described in the last sentence, "I cannot be precise as to the number of dead that I saw but it was at least tens of people." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And then in your transcript earlier today -- now I lost it, I'm sorry. Here we go. Page 9, starting on line 22. You made specific descriptions of what you saw in your testimony; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I will read portions of it to you. At line -- at page 10, line 4, you stated, "They were all shot at close range. I'm not saying by whom. I'm saying they were shot at close range. The two I refer to just now were shot through the head. We found a shallow grave with a man with his hands tied behind his back was shot through the head." Those are pretty specific recollections; are they not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And they stuck with you, did they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like the usher to please pull up 65 ter 04830. And with the assistance of the usher, I'd like to give Mr. Dreyer a copy of this statement. Actually, it's the wrong statement, I'm sorry. 04841.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, is this an earlier statement of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, the Chamber wondered what to do with paragraph 22 of the present statement where it refers to an earlier statement clarifies all kinds of things, the Chamber has no knowledge whatsoever about the earlier statement so therefore, it's not especially helpful, but we'll now get a glance at an earlier statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, you have that statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's the wrong one. Actually if I could have that one back. I'm sorry. Sorry, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be put on the ELMO so we can see it as well and that the witness, if it's zoomed in properly, that he can look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, I had asked for it to be pulled up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a mistake. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do we need it on the ELMO, Your Honour? I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we don't need it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to give it to the witness so he could follow along. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, you have that interview in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The date on the interview on the cover page is -- there are two interviews, the first is November 8th, 1995, some three months after Operation Storm; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the second interview which comprises this statement was on February 4th of 1996, some six months after Operation Storm; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And on the last page, if that could be pulled up, please. You signed that on February 4th, 1996; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the page before which is page 4 of the statement, at the bottom of that statement, you say, "This statement" -- or it's written, "This statement was recorded by me at sector west HQ Daruvar on the 4th of February 1996 at 1600 hours." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Where is Daruvar? Is that in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time -- yeah, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you were interviewed in Croatia three months after and six months after Operation Storm when you signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I was not interviewed -- the second statement was recorded by myself in my office in Daruvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you recorded it on a tape and sent to back to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have the original written statement?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I typed it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you typed -- this is in your typewriter, you did this yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just look again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. Other than the second page.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Other than the second page which appears to be handwritten.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's certainly my -- what I wrote. Whether it was -- but it was certainly not -- I was not interviewed in Daruvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. You typed this yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very -- the content, yes, whether it was laid out like this by myself, I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you were interviewed over the phone?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was interviewed for the first time in person in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In November of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first date, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Why don't we go to page 2 of that statement, Mr. Dreyer. This is the statement that you signed on February 4th of 1996 which comprised the results of two separate interviews in 1995 and 1996. You again toward the bottom of that page in the paragraph that starts, "At about ..." if you could go down to the third sentence that starts, "At about 1000 hours ..." You talk about the mortar round incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you talk about the body bag incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just reading, please. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Nowhere in this statement is a discussion of the tens of people that you saw on the 9th; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The bottom of page 2, you describe the civilian situation in Knin before offensive and on the second-last line, you state, "Front line soldiers could be seen at the coffee shops and old people walking around." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So there were front line soldiers in and about Knin at the time, from your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the page 3 of your statement, if you'd go there. Under military situation. The second sentence, "During the day, a substantial amount of soldiers could have been seen in town due to the rotation programme." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What is the rotation programme?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall what I referred to there. I would presume that there was soldiers coming and soldiers going out and I presume that's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So if that's what you were referring to and earlier you said if it's not in your statement, you didn't see it, in your earlier testimony, that rotation program would be something that was a military thing; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, can you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please use your microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you again use your microphone because it's not on, but perhaps other microphones are on which ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, Your Honour. I'll try again. Similar objection to the one I made before. I think the witness's previous reference, if I recall correctly, was to a specific question and a specific subject matter. I think this may be used at the moment as an all-encompassing qualification about the statement. I think it just needs to be made clear so the witness is aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, isn't it true that apart from that rereading your sentence, it's not entirely clear but -- if you please just ask the witness what --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I will do that Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what he knows and what he has seen. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of page 3, you note in your statement, "During 4 August 1995, I only observed about three to five dead bodies in the street, all civilians." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And this was again the statement that was given three and six months after Operation Storm; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like, if you would, Mr. -- I'd like to move this statement into evidence, Your Honour. I need a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could just have one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The same problem with the microphone. I switched mine off earlier so that yours would do, but now it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In any event, Your Honour, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D109.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D109 admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, I'd like you to go back to P72, the 2008 statement, page 3, note number 9.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Note number 9 it says, "For all the above reasons, it can be said that the fire on both 4 and 5 August was indiscriminate." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to go back to D109, your statement given three and six months after Operation Storm. You make no such conclusion in the statement that you gave three and six months after Operation Storm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll have to read the whole statement, but if you say -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If you want to read it to confirm it you, you may, but I can tell you that no such conclusion is made in D109.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a question the Chamber could answer as well by reviewing that statement whether it's in that statement or not. In general, there is no need to put questions to a witness where the answer, whatever it is, is clear, whatever the witness says. For example, if you ask whether the 3rd of February is less than three months ago then if the witness says no, then of course the Chamber would not accept that as a no. Of course if there's any reason to doubt the date on which the statement was given, but these are the kind of ritual dances which apparently are practised in some jurisdictions and while we often can do without --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand, I understand. I'm not a good dancer either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you could please pull up 65 ter 04830. And Mr. Usher, I have a copy for the witness -- the right one, this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, you have that statement in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's on the -- on the cover page, it's dated November 8th, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Three months after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, you certainly remember what I just said, unnecessary questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 2 of that document was signed by you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it was signed at Sector South HQ Knin on 8 November 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, you mentioned earlier on page 2 in the middle paragraph the fourth sentence that starts, "At about 1000 hours ..." are you there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that the same page, page 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. "At about 1000 hours whilst civilians ..."

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's the mortar incident you mentioned in your first statement and in your last statement; correct? Meaning that this incident is contained in all three statements, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the body bag incident further down is contained in all three statements; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yet the sighting of tens of dead is not included in this statement of November 8th, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, I think there may be some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, a microphone problem. Could someone else switch his microphone off so that Mr. Tieger's voice could be heard?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems to be in a couple of questions about that incident an attempt to link or consolidate the reference to tens of dead with the incident by the compound on August 5th and I don't think the statement makes that link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, would you agree that the tens are not related to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I agree. My whole point, Your Honour, is that this recollection in such detail was not made three months, six months, and two years after the incident, and it's been made here today at trial and three months ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that was the five to ten, isn't it? But you are now referring to the tens which appears somewhere else in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore if you would link them, should it at least be clear and that the witness should not be taken by surprise that what he earlier said was about the tens of dead related to that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure, Your Honour, I guess I'll go back again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: To page 6 of P72, Mr. Dreyer, which is your February 21 and 22, 2008 statement?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This incident in paragraph 22 you would agree with me, would you not, was not described in your previous two statements; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see, 22 of the February 08 statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 22 -- you said this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Described in paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there one incident described or is there -- I do see that one day after we were let out of the UN compound, and finding many dead civilians ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that's where we are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's 22 for me but perhaps it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 22 of P72.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's the February 2008 statement, Your Honour, paragraph 22 begins "Although I cannot recall the specific dates, I do recall ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Now where is the exact incident? Is it "Finding many dead civilians ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, "most of which had been shot at close range."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that -- I'm a bit confused. Is that the same incident as the mortal shell?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is not. It is not and the witness can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It says something about finding dead bodies, not about that they were all shot at one incident, were they? At least that's not what I can read there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We're talking about two different things, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The mortar incident and the body bag incident are consistent throughout all three statements and in this statement of February of 2008 it's described in paragraph 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 22, there is a new incident now in which the witness states that there were men and women all shot at close range. They were not wearing military uniforms and they -- he cannot be precise to the number because it was at least tens of people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The confusion is that you are referring to an incident where what I see here is that you find a number of bodies which are not necessarily part of one incident, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least it's not described as an incident, it's described as finding a number of bodies and some conclusions drawn to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm winding up here Judge but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but we -- may I take it, Mr. Tieger, that you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have one matter very quickly in redirect. I think we can send the witness home today and I'd really urge the Court to do that since Mr. Kuzmanovic is winding up he's aware of my concerns about time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then of course I have to avoid further troubles with other Trial Chambers. Let me just ask the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are under some pressure. Mr. Kuzmanovic, three minutes would do?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That will do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, the November 8th of 1995 statement, if you could get that in front of you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That document is also -- is silent about indiscriminate artillery fire, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's silent about what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Indiscriminate artillery fire; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I resolve this, please, quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic said it's also silent about artillery indiscriminate artillery fire, D109, the statement that he referred to earlier says at page 3, and that's the statement that was signed in February of 1996, "For all of the above reasons it can be said that the fire was indiscriminate." Perhaps we can just eliminate these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, any need to put further questions as what appears and what does not appear in this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No, there isn't, Your Honour. It is silent as to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is on page 3, Your Honour, and I would ask Mr. Kuzmanovic to look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try -- Mr. Tieger, you are not supposed to give the answers to the questions, but if it is on page 3, Mr. Kuzmanovic, which I did not check, then of course there's no need to put this question to the witness. If it's not, then as I said before, whether something is in or is not in a statement, the parties could even agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure. I don't have a problem with that, the 8th of November interview 65 ter 04830 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties are invited to get together and to see whether the indiscriminate fire appears in this statement, yes or no. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell Your Honour it does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger says it does, so therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but my point was is it was referred to -- Mr. Kuzmanovic said also, meaning he was referring back to the February 1996 statement about which he asked earlier and suggested that there was no reference to indiscriminate fire in that statement. There is such a reference at page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The parties are invited to agree on whether the word indiscriminate fire appears in these statements and if they cannot agree on that, I will certainly be available to assist them at meetings 7.00 in the morning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm done. I would just like to admit this last November 8th, 1995 statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D110.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D110 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will just move quickly through redirect, if I may Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, very quickly, Mr. Kehoe asked you reporting back at the end of your second trip and that begins towards the end of page 56, continues on to page 57. You indicated the timing of that trip and then you were asked at approximately 5620 or so when you got back and again that's a reference to the second trip, did you report to anyone? And then you said, "It says in my statement here that I went back to the bunker and discussed with the sector commander and Chief of Staff." You were referring back to your statement. Can I direct your attention back to your statement at page 4, ask you to look at the last sentence under the paragraph regarding the first trip which says, "In the bunker I liaised with the sector commander and the sector administration officer and informed them of the delinquency of our first attempt." And the next paragraph 13 contains the reference to the second trip which does not have a similar reference to the bunker and liaising with the sector commander and the sector administration officer and so on. When you were referring back to your statement to indicate to you reported to was that at the end of the first trip or the second trip?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I reported at the return of each trip, I reported back on our progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Judge Kinis has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement 2008, you mentioned in paragraph 3, you mentioned that during the day, a substantial amount of soldiers could have been seen in the town. Could you please clarify this issue?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. When I referred to the substantial amount of soldiers that could be seen in town, Knin was generally seen from our perspective as the rest and recuperation location, so the soldiers that was observed in town were seen as clearly soldiers but unarmed. They were there on their R and R. That's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question for you as well. Could P64 be put on the screen. This document has been shown to you before today and I would also like you to focus on paragraph 2 of this document which is an assessment of the damage. It reads, "The damages caused by shelling to civilian establishments is concentrate to the close vicinity of military objectives. Only few (3-5) impacts is observed in other urban areas." Now, we went in quite some detail through the itineraries you took at this day. This assessment, do you consider that in view of the observations you made, an accurate assessment of the damage which was done to urban areas not close to military objectives, and I would like you, for answering this question, to accept the suggestion or the assumption by the Defence on what military objectives were. Would you consider, on the basis of this assumption, this to be an accurate description of the damage to civilian areas?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the -- what was presented in the red was indeed military objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the part of the city that was the most intense bombarded during that day, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But now, I'm asking you mainly about areas which -- and it says here "Three to five impacts is observed in other urban areas." That is urban areas not close to military targets.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the map, Your Honour, I would not necessarily agree with that fully. They were on the ground looking at it, so I presume that the statement over there is correct, but certainly where we were driving and the areas where we were collecting UN staff members, there was shelling or the impact of shelling wherever we went, as indicated on my map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And urban areas, you indicated on these maps where there were portions of your itinerary where you didn't see any of the suggested military targets very nearby. Would you agree then that there were very few impacts, three to five, in those portions of the -- that you saw?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say few impacts. Three to five, Your Honour, I can't say, but I said fewer than in the areas that were indicated with yellow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's basically answered. Thank you very much. Any need for further questions caused by the questions by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, if I could have just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you urged the Chamber to release the witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour. Okay, okay. Just one point of clarification, Mr. Dreyer -- I'm sorry about the delay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, in the appendices and the exhibits you provided you indicated areas where you saw shelling and some of the specific impacts you observed. Some of those areas as you saw were in the vicinities where the Defence asserted there were military targets and some of those areas were outside those areas where the Defence had indicated there were military targets; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you just indicated to the Court, you observed more concentrated fire in the area where they indicated there was military targets, but you also observed shelling everywhere you went that day?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIES DREYER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object, Judge. That's not what he just said. I mean he answered Your Honour's question specifically on this particular score, that in the area and counsel is leading the witness and trying to put words in his mouth, and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- well, to some extent he did. To some extent he also reflected what the witness said earlier. That's a matter also of consistency in the testimony. Let's be quite clear, Mr. Dreyer. What this Chamber would like to know and what apparently Mr. Tieger wanted to find out is whether, in the areas where there were no military targets, as far as the Defence tells us, whether what, approximately, the number of damaged -- impacts were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I could see, we were under a great amount of pressure while we were driving around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What we could have seen that there was certainly at the areas indicated in yellow, where the military targets were supposed to be there was a concentration of fire but in civilian areas outside where there was not indicative of yellow military targets, there was also but not as intense as the areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if also -- you said three to five, not necessarily. Could you be more precise? If not, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot be more precise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You cannot be more precise. Then that's clear. Mr. Tieger, may I take it that this answers also your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Mr. Dreyer, this concludes your testimony in this court. We'd like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague and for having answered questions of the parties and questions of the Bench. Yes, Mr. -- Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just -- I'm sorry, just to clarify because I apologise very much for this but I just want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you refer -- if you would like to refer to what the witness said before and that's what you apparently did, you should quote him literally. I don't know whether it was a literal quote or not, I did not verify that, so therefore we will be very critical of any question you would like to put to the witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dreyer, in the areas where you indicated shelling on your aerial maps, both in the appendices and elsewhere, I know you indicated both specific impacts locations that you recalled and areas where shelling occurred. In the areas where you indicated shelling occurred, was there at least one shell impact in those areas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, I object. This was all on direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is also a question which doesn't need an answer because if you design an area where for shell impact then it means that at least there should be one, isn't it? And then Mr. Tieger, I see you are counting number of areas, one, two, three, four, five, I take it that that's what you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just trying to clarify this. I think there is a suggestion here that maybe in the areas outside the areas where the yellow pin points were, there may have been only three to five impacts and I'm asking the witness if that's the case or if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the clue is the word "vicinity." That's the clue and that might be one of the problems, what is still in the vicinity of and what is not. I did not understand this witness to say that in the areas he marked, that there was no shell impact at all. He had specific ones and in areas, I do understand, that there was at least one impact. Mr. Dreyer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was your last question, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I wanted to ask –

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't have to comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I wanted to ask him if in some instances there were more and if so, how many more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we want to go back through the whole direct and cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we have heard the witness and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I started saying to Mr. Dreyer that he has concluded his testimony and that I'd like to thank him not only for answering the questions put to him by the parties and by the Bench but also the additional question put to him by Mr. Tieger and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Usher, could you escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have no witness for tomorrow. However, we have an MFI list still to be dealt with. Now, there are two ways of doing that. That is to come to court tomorrow all of us, interpreters, security, everyone, and deal with it there or to see whether there's a possibility that we -- that there is an agreement about what objections there still are, what translations we are still waiting for and are not -- however, I like it to be all 40 of us in court. So therefore I suggest that we make an attempt this afternoon to see how far we come in that respect and that we would not then sit tomorrow which would mean that we would then adjourn but under this proviso until Monday, the 21st of April, 9.00 in the morning. Mr. Registrar, would this be the same courtroom? It would be Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
